_: THE MCP-ELICITATION PARITY CORPUS. One file, two readers: server/tests/elicitation_parity.rs (sessions::elicitation) and web/tests/unit/chat-elicitation-parity.test.ts (components/chat/elicitation.ts). Every `payload` is an `Elicitation` hook payload in Claude Code 2.1.227's documented shape - `Input to command is JSON with mcp_server_name, message, and requested_schema` (bundle strings; the same doc block that defines the ElicitationResult leg as mcp_server_name/action/content/mode/elicitation_id, and warns that this hook's STDOUT answers the form). Fields: name; source; payload; expect (null when the ask must be REFUSED, else server/message/id/dropped_fields and the typed `fields` the schema becomes - a SUBSET, every key listed must match); cases (value sets and the exact per-field complaints both validators must produce, using Claude Code's own sentences). Why a shared file: the form is validated TWICE - in the browser while somebody types, and again on the server before an answer could ever be delivered - and neither language errors when the two drift. Before this corpus existed neither plane knew elicitation happened at all: the hook was not installed, nothing reaches the transcript, and an MCP-using session parked on the dialog forever wearing a green Idle dot.
